summary: Describes using the ATM Frame User Network Interface (FUNI) to frame PPP-encapsulated packets, so PPP can run over FUNI links.

subtitle: How to carry PPP frames over an ATM FUNI virtual connection, with two ways to tag the payload.

tldr.problem: PPP usually frames its packets with HDLC, but some point-to-point links are ATM virtual connections using the Frame User Network Interface (FUNI). PPP needs a defined way to ride on them.
tldr.mechanism: PPP packets are placed in the User SDU field of a FUNI frame, either bare (VC-multiplexed) or behind an LLC header and NLPID byte (LLC encapsulated). Switched circuits signal the choice in a Q.2931 B-LLI element.
tldr.outcome: Both ends can use the full PPP toolbox (LCP, NCPs, authentication, compression) over FUNI, provided they agree on the encapsulation and follow the LCP option rules.

today: RFC 2363 is a Proposed Standard published in July 1998, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: PPP Meets FUNI
sections.content:
The ATM FUNI (Frame User Network Interface) protocol provides virtual connections between end stations on the same network. It offers a packet delivery service with error detection but no error correction. Most PPP implementations use ISO 3309 HDLC for framing; when an ATM network is configured with point-to-point connections, PPP can use FUNI as its framing mechanism instead.

PPP sees the FUNI layer as a bit-synchronous point-to-point link, and one PPP link corresponds to one FUNI virtual connection. That connection MUST be full-duplex and point to point, and it MAY be dedicated (permanent, set up by provisioning) or switched (set up on demand). The interface is an octet interface with no sub-octets, and PPP puts no limit on transmission rate. The FUNI layer MUST give PPP control signals saying when the connection is connected or disconnected, which become the "Up" and "Down" events of the LCP state machine.

The RFC is aimed at implementations that want PPP facilities such as the Link Control Protocol, Network-layer Control Protocols, authentication and compression. These need a point-to-point relationship between peers and are not designed for the multi-point relationships ATM can also offer.
sections.eli5: Two computers share a private ATM line, and PPP is their way of talking. This RFC says how to treat that line like a simple wire between them, and tells PPP when the line is plugged in or unplugged.

sections.title: Two Ways to Identify the Payload
sections.content:
The RFC builds on the principles and frame structure of RFC 1483 (Multiprotocol Interconnect over AAL5). That document defines two ways to say what protocol a payload carries. With virtual circuit multiplexing, the two ends agree on the protocol for each circuit, through provisioning or control-plane procedures. With LLC encapsulation, each PDU carries an in-band LLC header naming the protocol.

An implementation carrying PPP over FUNI MUST support both: VC-multiplexed PPP and LLC encapsulated PPP on PVCs, chosen by mutual configuration or negotiation. For switched circuits it MUST negotiate using the Q.2931 Annex C procedure, encoding a B-LLI information element to signal which one is wanted.

One exception: an implementation connecting through a Frame Relay/ATM FRF.8 interworking unit to an RFC 1973 end point MUST use LLC encapsulated PPP. Such interworking units are exempt from supporting VC-multiplexed PPP.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to label a parcel: agree beforehand that everything on this road is PPP, or stick a label on every parcel. Both ends must know how to do both, and must agree on which one to use.

sections.title: VC-Multiplexed PPP Frames
sections.content:
A FUNI PDU starts and ends with a flag. Inside are a FUNI Header, a User SDU and a FUNI FCS of 2 or 4 octets. The header holds a 10-bit or 24-bit Frame Address (also called the VPI/VCI bits), a Congestion Notification bit, a Congestion Loss Priority bit and four Reserved bits. The User SDU carries up to 4096 octets, optionally up to 64K. The FCS protects the whole FUNI PDU except the FCS itself.

In VC-multiplexed mode a PPP frame is the User SDU: a Protocol ID of 8 or 16 bits, then the Information field, then padding. These fields are defined in RFC 1661. Nothing else is added, because both ends already know the circuit carries PPP.
sections.eli5: The envelope has a stamp, an address and a check mark. Because everyone knows this road only carries PPP mail, the PPP letter goes straight inside with no extra label.

sections.title: LLC Encapsulated PPP Frames
sections.content:
In LLC mode the User SDU begins with a short header. The LLC header has destination SAP 0xFE, source SAP 0xFE (a routed OSI PDU) and frame type UI 0x03. Next comes the NLPID for PPP, 0xCF. After that is the PPP protocol identifier (1 or 2 octets), the PPP information field and padding, then the FUNI FCS of 2 or 4 octets.

The two ends MAY be bilaterally provisioned to send other LLC-encapsulated protocols over the same virtual connection. However, they MUST NOT send packets of any protocol that has an active NCP within the PPP session. Implementations SHOULD schedule packets so the quality of service commitments of both the PPP and non-PPP flows are affected as little as possible.
sections.eli5: Here every PPP letter gets a small label first that says "this is PPP". That way the same road could also carry other kinds of mail, as long as PPP is not already handling that kind.

sections.title: Signaling for Switched Circuits
sections.content:
When a caller sets up a switched virtual circuit, its SETUP message MUST request VC-multiplexed PPP, LLC-encapsulated PPP, or both. If it offers both, the two B-LLI information elements go inside a Broadband Repeat Indicator IE in order of preference. The called side MUST accept an incoming call that offers LLC-encapsulated PPP, and MUST reject a call that offers only an encapsulation it does not support. A caller offering both MUST be able to negotiate LLC-encapsulated PPP.

For a VC-multiplexed call, the Q.2931 B-LLI user information layer 3 protocol field selects ISO/IEC TR 9577 in octet 7, with an IPI value of PPP (0xCF). For an LLC call, the layer 2 protocol field selects LAN Logical Link Control (ISO/IEC8802-2) in octet 6; RFC 1755 appendix A has an example.
sections.eli5: When you phone someone to set up a line, you say which labelling style you can use, in order of preference. The other side says no if it cannot use any of them.

sections.title: Unexpected Encapsulation Changes
sections.content:
If a virtual connection loses state, one side may unilaterally switch between VC-multiplexed and LLC encapsulation. The RFC defines detection and recovery for both directions. With LLC encapsulation, the first six octets of an LCP packet, which are also the first six octets of the FUNI frame, are fe-fe-03-cf-c0-21. With VC-multiplexing the initial LCP packet starts with c0-21 right after the FUNI Header.

Once PPP is in the Network-layer Protocol phase and has negotiated an NCP, a frame in the other, equivalent encapsulation MUST trigger action. On an SVC the call is cleared at once with cause value 111, "protocol error, unspecified". On a PVC the link tears down the active NCPs, SHOULD generate an error message, enters the Termination state and silently drops all received packets. These rules prevent "black-holes" when a peer loses state.
sections.eli5: If one side forgets which labelling style was agreed and starts using the other, the line is cut or reset so that nobody keeps sending letters into the void.

sections.title: LCP Option Rules
sections.content:
The Magic Number LCP option is RECOMMENDED and Protocol Field Compression is NOT RECOMMENDED. An implementation MUST NOT request, and MUST reject a request for, the Field Check Sequence (FCS) Alternatives, Address-and-Control-Field-Compression (ACFC) and Asynchronous-Control-Character-Map (ACCM) options.

The Maximum-Receive-Unit option MUST NOT be negotiated larger than the maximum CPCS-SDU size in the associated direction of the circuit's traffic contract. If a PPP link is bridged across several physical sections, the LCP framing options MUST be negotiated independently on each FUNI section. When a PVC is in the Stopped state, the implementation is RECOMMENDED to wait for Configure-Requests.
sections.eli5: This RFC says not to ask for a few of PPP's usual settings here. It also says never to promise bigger packets than the line allows.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
ATM networks are virtual circuit based, so security is implicit in how the provider administers PVCs between network boundaries. The chance of a breach from mis-routed ATM cells is considered negligible.

With switched circuits the model resembles dial-up over the telephone network, and the same PAP and CHAP authentication used for Internet dial-up applies, giving security on par with existing practice. Applications needing more are encouraged to use authentication headers, encrypted payloads and/or ATM-layer security services. With LLC-encapsulated PPP, an end point cannot assume PPP authentication also secures the other LLC flows on the same virtual connection.
sections.eli5: A private ATM line is hard to tap by accident, and PPP's usual password checks still work. Mail of other kinds sharing the line is not covered by those checks.
